alignments.note: Privative adjective rendered by a negated verb phrase; the head stands on the word glossing the stem, not on the negation that spells the alpha-privative (rule 84).
Genitive-absolute participle with the supplied subordinator 'Seeing' and its complementizer 'that' (rules 7, 86); no other English word realizes the participle.
τούτων → 'these things'; the generic noun expands the demonstrative and the demonstrative keeps the head (rule 17).
The periphrasis δέον ἐστίν is compressed into the single modal 'ought'; part of that word answers to the participle carrying the necessity, so the pair is one aligned unit (rule 39's test).
ὑμᾶς → 'ye', recast as the English subject.
ὑπάρχειν → 'to be'; the infinitival marker is its own helper (rules 7, 61).
πράσσειν → 'to do'; the repeated infinitival marker is a rule 7 helper on the verb it introduces.

review_notes: δέον ἐστίν is joined into one aligned unit on 'ought' rather than leaving the copula unrepresented; splitting them would leave one token with no English word at all.
ἀναντιρρήτων → 'cannot be gainsaid' is headed on 'gainsaid' under rule 84's reasoning for a privative.
